  • It also makes technical adjustments to numerous municipal charters and related acts.
Part 1 Cities and Towns Act / Municipal Code
  • Allows municipalities to acquire buildings whose taxes have been unpaid for at least 3 years.
  • Allows the sale of small parcels of land to neighbouring owners.
  • Expands municipalities' power to purchase or build buildings for rental purposes.
  • Adjusts the publicity rules for property leased or sold by municipalities.
  • Standardizes the powers of municipal directors general and the rules for calling council meetings.
Part 2 Act respecting land use planning and development
  • Clarifies what a municipal building by-law may include, particularly regarding the energy efficiency of buildings.
Part 3 Regulation respecting the maximum non-taxable value of certain presbyteries
  • Abolishes the exemption from municipal and school property taxes for certain presbyteries.
Part 4 Act respecting duties on transfers of immovables
  • Introduces an exemption from the transfer duty for certain transfers between undivided co-owners.
Part 5 Act respecting municipal taxation
  • Adjusts the rules for preparing the general collection roll.
Part 6 Cities and Towns Act
  • Removes the cap applicable to the amounts a municipality may set aside in a financial reserve.
  • Adjusts the rules on municipal borrowing and the delegation of functions to the executive committee.
Part 7 Act respecting the prohibition on municipal subsidies
  • Clarifies that non-profit organizations are not commercial or industrial establishments.
Part 8 Charters of Montréal and Québec
  • Contain specific measures unique to these two cities.
  • Various related charters, orders and acts (Gatineau, Lévis, Longueuil, Laval, Saguenay, Shawinigan, La Tuque, metropolitan communities, transit corporations, Commission municipale): consistency adjustments related to the changes above.

27343:
• This bill covers two main areas: collective agreement decrees and the construction industry, amending 19 laws and regulations.
  • It strengthens the powers of the Minister of Labour and eases certain administrative obligations of joint committees.
Part 1 Act respecting collective agreement decrees
  • The Minister now directly decrees the amendments requested by a joint committee or a contracting party.
  • The Minister may approve, amend or repeal regulations made by joint committees.
  • A uniform process allows the renewal of a decree to be prevented through a notice sent to the Minister in the sixth month preceding the decree's expiry.
  • The Minister must assess the representativeness of employer and union associations before recommending an extension or amendment of a decree.
  • The Minister may issue directives on the sound governance of joint committees, including on inspection matters.
  • Ends the obligation to publish a notice in newspapers acknowledging receipt of a request for extension or amendment.
  • Ends the annual obligation of joint committees to submit budget forecasts and audited financial statements to the Minister.
  • Ends the requirement to be recognized as a training mutual in order to receive workforce training subsidies.
Part 2 Act respecting labour standards
  • New enabling provision allowing the government to establish sectoral standards for workers and employers in a sector whose decree has expired.
Part 3 Act respecting labour relations... (construction)
  • Specifies the working conditions and benefits of health and safety representatives on construction sites.
  • Sets the conditions for deploying or withdrawing health and safety representatives and coordinators at the start and completion of work, without regard to the total cost of the work.
  • A prime contractor must notify representative associations when a full-time health and safety representative must be designated.
  • Excludes from its scope permanent employees of the Société des établissements de plein air du Québec, housing cooperatives and non-profit housing organizations.
  • The government may launch pilot projects to study or improve the standards applicable in the industry.
  • The Commission de la construction du Québec will be able to create a supplementary preventive withdrawal plan for pregnant or breastfeeding workers, administered by the Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail.
  • The Commission de la construction du Québec may grant temporary work authorizations providing the same rights as a competency certificate, according to its own criteria.
  • Act respecting occupational health and safety, Act respecting industrial accidents and occupational diseases, Regulation respecting prevention mechanisms and various sectoral decrees: concordance adjustments related to the above changes.
  • The bill also provides for transitional and final provisions for the implementation of these changes.

27345:
• Creates a new Self-Directed Personal Assistance Program with financial assistance, administered by Retraite Québec.

• The bill creates a new right allowing a person who is worried to obtain information about an intimate partner who may pose a risk to their safety.
  • It establishes a comprehensive process involving the Sûreté du Québec and a designated body to handle these requests and disclose the information.
  • New act respecting the disclosure of information: a person at risk, or someone acting on their behalf with their consent, may request information about their intimate partner.
  • New act: a minor aged 14 or over may submit such a request on their own.
  • New act: the government may, by regulation, designate other persons or categories of persons who may submit a request.
  • New act: police officers and workers from support organizations may inform a person at risk about the request process if it could benefit them.
  • New act: a police officer may, in these cases, disclose the identity of the partner who is the subject of a possible request.
  • New act: the Sûreté du Québec conducts the searches and transmits the relevant information to a body designated by the minister responsible for the status of women.
  • New act: a designated person, subject to regulatory conditions, meets with the person at risk to verbally communicate the information or the absence of relevant information.
  • New act: this person may also direct the person at risk to specialized resources and provide additional information.
  • New act: restrictions govern the disclosure to the intimate partner of the existence of a request and personal information concerning them.
  • New act: rules limit the further communication and use of the information obtained.
  • New act: certain persons benefit from immunity for acts performed in the exercise of their duties related to this process.
  • New act: these persons cannot be compelled to testify before a court concerning this information.
  • New act: penal offences are provided for breaches of the rules on communication or use of information.
  • Act respecting the Québec correctional system: revises the rules on disclosing to victims information concerning incarcerated persons or those under the supervision of correctional services.
  • Act respecting the Ministère de la Sécurité publique: consequential adjustments related to the creation of the new information disclosure regime.
